title: A brim that rises
summary: After a tip, lift the brim for a while. That lift outlasts the leak.

cards.text:
The water forgets quickly.
A brim that jumps up after a tip, then sinks slowly, remembers longer.

The tips write that slow memory themselves.
You can teach the wires with the diary from earlier.

question.prompt: A bucket whose only memory is a fast leak can hold a one-second pause.
question.why: The leak is gone long before the second is up.
question.simpler: You need a slower dial than the hole.

question.prompt: What writes the slow memory here?
choices: An outside notebook with no tips
question.why: Each tip lifts the brim. The lift fades on its own clock.
question.simpler: This is not the frozen pond. These wires are taught.

recall.question: Why can a rising brim remember longer than the leak?
recall.answer: It is a second, slower state written by the tips.

deeper.note: Bellec and colleagues trained recurrent spiking nets with that adaptive brim. The paper’s second half is learning-to-learn. The brim is enough for today. In snnTorch the recurrent bucket is RLeaky. The rising brim is extra.

paper.title: Long short-term memory and learning-to-learn in networks of spiking neurons
paper.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
paper.section: The adaptive neuron and the memory tasks.

terms.plain: the threshold lifts after a spike
terms.definition: A slow state that raises the firing threshold after each spike, giving memory longer than the membrane leak.
